2. Let $P(G)$ be the probability a student likes green: $0.45$.
3. Let $P(B \cap G)$ be the probability a student likes both: $0.22$.

The probability that a student likes either blue or green (or both) is:
$P(B \cup G) = P(B) + P(G) - P(B \cap G)$
$P(B \cup G) = 0.58 + 0.45 - 0.22 = 0.81$

The probability that a student likes neither is the complement of the probability that they like at least one:
$P(\text{Neither}) = 1 - P(B \cup G)$
$P(\text{Neither}) = 1 - 0.81 = 0.19$
